title: Lakehouse Zero Copy: Iceberg Federation vs Bulk JDBC Copy

steps.prompt: A company keeps 100TB of telemetry in Databricks as Apache Iceberg tables (Parquet). Product wants Data 360 insights on that telemetry without paying to duplicate the lake into Salesforce storage. Which approach is Well-Architected?

options.label: File-based Zero Copy federation via Iceberg REST Catalog metadata so Data 360 queries Parquet/Iceberg in place
options.rationale: Data 360 file federation for lakehouses relies on Apache Iceberg tabular metadata and Parquet files exposed through an Iceberg REST Catalog — enabling governed zero-copy access without moving 100TB.

options.label: Nightly JDBC extract that copies all 100TB into Data 360 DLOs for "local performance"
options.rationale: Bulk-copying a 100TB lake defeats Zero Copy economics: it multiplies storage cost, extends ingest windows, and creates freshness lag versus federated query.

options.label: Hourly SFTP drops of CSV extracts into a ContentVersion staging object
options.rationale: CSV/SFTP polling lacks lakehouse metadata federation, is high-latency, and is a poor fit for analytical telemetry at this scale.
